claim: At 24 hours post-fertilisation (hpf), transcripts for cdh17 are down-regulated in the posterior most portion of the DE segment.
source: We found that at 24 hr post-fertilisation (hpf), transcripts for cdh17 are down-regulated in the posterior most portion of the DE segment (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: The first stc1+ cells appear in the posterior most portion of the DE segment at 24 hpf and increase in number.
source: Concomitant with this, the first stc1+ cells appear in this region and increase in number.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: By 32 hpf the stc1+ cells appear as a prominent bulge on the dorsal side of the tubule.
source: By 32 hpf the stc1+ + appear as a prominent bulge on the dorsal side of the tubule and at 50 hpf, they are found as discrete, and separate, structures on top of each pronephric tubule in ~70% of animals (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and live imaging data shown in Figure 1A and 1C.

claim: At 50 hpf, stc1+ cells are found as discrete, and separate, structures on top of each pronephric tubule in ~70% of animals.
source: By 32 hpf the stc1+ + appear as a prominent bulge on the dorsal side of the tubule and at 50 hpf, they are found as discrete, and separate, structures on top of each pronephric tubule in ~70% of animals (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C histogram.

claim: CS cells arise from renal epithelial cells via transdifferentiation and are then physically extruded from the tubule.
source: These observations suggest that CS cells arise from renal epithelial cells via transdifferentiation and are then physically extruded from the tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed expression patterns and morphological changes described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Presumptive CS cells bulge out of the dorsal wall of the tubule concomitant with the constriction of their apical membranes.
source: Presumptive CS cells were observed to bulge out of the dorsal wall of the tubule concomitant with the constriction of their apical membranes.
evidence: The claim is supported by live time-lapse imaging data described in the text and shown in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: CS cells adopt a wedge shape with narrowed apical membranes marked by Phalloidin+ F-actin.
source: Immunostaining of sagittal cross-sections through the CS region at this stage showed that the cells adopt a wedge shape with narrowed apical membranes (marked by Phalloidin+ F-actin, Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: As apical constriction increases, adjacent non-CS epithelial cells move closer together and CS cells protrude dorsally as an arch two cell layers wide.
source: As apical constriction increased, we observed that the adjacent non-CS epithelial cells moved closer together and the CS cells protruded dorsally as an arch two cell layers wide (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The epithelial cells on either side of the CS cells eventually meet at 42 hpf in most animals, followed by extrusion of the CS gland from the tubule.
source: The epithelial cells on either side of the CS cells eventually met at 42 hpf in most animals, followed by extrusion of the CS gland from the tubule (Figure 1A and Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: The timing of CS cell extrusion is variable but is complete in the majority of embryos by 60 hpf.
source: The timing of extrusion was variable but was complete in the majority of embryos by 60 hpf (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C histogram.

claim: During extrusion from the tubule, the epithelial cell adhesion molecule gene (epcam) remains continuously expressed in CS cells.
source: We found that during extrusion from the tubule, the epithelial cell adhesion molecule gene (epcam) remains continuously expressed in CS cells (Figure 1E) and the major epithelial cell adhesion protein Cadherin-1 (Cdh1) is retained on the basolateral membranes (Figure 1D), suggesting that the epithelial status of CS cells is not changed during extrusion.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The major epithelial cell adhesion protein Cadherin-1 (Cdh1) is retained on the basolateral membranes during CS cell extrusion.
source: We found that during extrusion from the tubule, the epithelial cell adhesion molecule gene (epcam) remains continuously expressed in CS cells (Figure 1E) and the major epithelial cell adhesion protein Cadherin-1 (Cdh1) is retained on the basolateral membranes (Figure 1D), suggesting that the epithelial status of CS cells is not changed during extrusion.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The epithelial status of CS cells is not changed during extrusion.
source: We found that during extrusion from the tubule, the epithelial cell adhesion molecule gene (epcam) remains continuously expressed in CS cells (Figure 1E) and the major epithelial cell adhesion protein Cadherin-1 (Cdh1) is retained on the basolateral membranes (Figure 1D), suggesting that the epithelial status of CS cells is not changed during extrusion.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the continuous expression of epithelial markers during extrusion.

claim: After CS cell extrusion, Cdh1 is detectable at the interface between CS and tubular cells and is prominent on the lateral membranes of CS cells.
source: After CS cell extrusion, Cdh1 is detectable at the interface between CS and tubular cells and is prominent on the lateral membranes of CS cells, similar to renal epithelial cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Once extruded, Cdh1 immunostaining is largely lost from the interface between CS cells and tubular cells but remains on the basal surface of some CS cells.
source: However, once extruded Cdh1 immunostaining is largely lost from the interface between CS cells and tubular cells but remains on the basal surface of some CS cells (Figure 1D, dotted box region).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: F-actin staining, which demarcates the apical surface of tubular cells, is lost in the extruded CS cells.
source: In addition, F-actin staining, which demarcates the apical surface of tubular cells, is lost in the extruded CS cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Renal epithelial cells transdifferentiate directly into CS cells, without a loss of epithelial character, extrude from the tubule following apical constriction, and form a distinct ball of unpolarised glandular epithelium.
source: These results suggest a model in which renal epithelial cells transdifferentiate directly into CS cells, without a loss of epithelial character, extrude from the tubule following apical constriction, and form a distinct ball of unpolarised glandular epithelium.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple observations including marker expression, cell morphology, and extrusion behavior.

claim: At 14 hpf, transcripts for lhx1a are found throughout the intermediate mesoderm in mesenchymal cells.
source: At 14 hpf, transcripts for lhx1a are found throughout the intermediate mesoderm in mesenchymal cells but are rapidly downregulated in all tubule precursors by 16 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), when the transition to an epithelial tube occurs (Gerlach and Wingert, 2014; Naylor et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcripts for lhx1a are rapidly downregulated in all tubule precursors by 16 hpf.
source: At 14 hpf, transcripts for lhx1a are found throughout the intermediate mesoderm in mesenchymal cells but are rapidly downregulated in all tubule precursors by 16 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), when the transition to an epithelial tube occurs (Gerlach and Wingert, 2014; Naylor et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and cited literature.

claim: The transition to an epithelial tube occurs at 16 hpf.
source: At 14 hpf, transcripts for lhx1a are found throughout the intermediate mesoderm in mesenchymal cells but are rapidly downregulated in all tubule precursors by 16 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), when the transition to an epithelial tube occurs (Gerlach and Wingert, 2014; Naylor et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Gerlach and Wingert, 2014; Naylor et al., 2016a).

claim: At 22 hpf, the DE segment contains apically localised F-actin and basally deposited Laminin and Collagen type IV.
source: To demonstrate that the tubule has achieved an advanced state of epithelial differentiation prior to stc1 transcripts appearing, we confirmed at 22 hpf that the DE segment contains apically localised F-actin and basally deposited Laminin and Collagen type IV, indicative of apical tight junctions and a basolateral basement membrane, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Apically localised F-actin and basally deposited Laminin and Collagen type IV are indicative of apical tight junctions and a basolateral basement membrane, respectively.
source: To demonstrate that the tubule has achieved an advanced state of epithelial differentiation prior to stc1 transcripts appearing, we confirmed at 22 hpf that the DE segment contains apically localised F-actin and basally deposited Laminin and Collagen type IV, indicative of apical tight junctions and a basolateral basement membrane, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about epithelial cell markers.

claim: At 22 hpf, the DE segment uniformly expresses slc12a1, atp1a1a.4 and krt18 (but not stc1).
source: In addition, the DE segment at this time point uniformly expresses slc12a1, atp1a1a.4 and the krt18 (but not stc1), consistent with having the identity of a differentiated transporting epithelium (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At 50 hpf, the DE segment continues to be marked by the expression of slc12a1, atp1a1a.4 and krt18 whereas the extruded CS cells do not express these genes.
source: At 50 hpf, the DE segment continues to be marked by the expression of slc12a1, atp1a1a.4 and krt18 whereas the extruded CS cells do not express these genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data described in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At 50 hpf, the CS gland has lost apically localised F-actin and is enveloped by a separate basement membrane.
source: Instead, staining with Phalloidin and antibodies to Laminin and Collagen type IV shows that the CS gland has lost apically localised F-actin and is enveloped by a separate basement membrane (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: By 22 hpf, the DE segment has differentiated into a renal tubular epithelium.
source: Taken together, these results support the notion that by 22 hpf, the DE segment has differentiated into a renal tubular epithelium, and that a subset of these cells then transdifferentiate into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple markers of epithelial differentiation.

claim: A subset of DE segment cells transdifferentiate into CS cells after 22 hpf.
source: Taken together, these results support the notion that by 22 hpf, the DE segment has differentiated into a renal tubular epithelium, and that a subset of these cells then transdifferentiate into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal sequence of marker expression and morphological changes.

claim: CS cells fail to extrude in all Blebbistatin-treated embryos (n = 57).
source: We found that the CS cells failed to extrude in all Blebbistatin-treated embryos (n = 57) and instead, stc1+ cells remained within the tubule (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Blebbistatin treatment shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In Blebbistatin-treated embryos, stc1+ cells remain within the tubule.
source: We found that the CS cells failed to extrude in all Blebbistatin-treated embryos (n = 57) and instead, stc1+ cells remained within the tubule (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Blebbistatin treatment shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Apical constriction of CS cells is a necessary prerequisite for extrusion from the renal tubule.
source: Thus we conclude that apical constriction of CS cells is a necessary prerequisite for extrusion from the renal tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the Blebbistatin treatment experiment that blocks apical constriction and prevents extrusion.

claim: CS cells only proliferate once they have been extruded from the tubule.
source: This analysis showed that CS cells only proliferate once they have been extruded from the tubule (n = 6 at each time-point, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Inhibition of proliferation between 20 hpf and 26 hpf with hydroxyurea and aphidicolin does not reduce the initial number of stc1+ cells that arise in the tubule.
source: Inhibition of proliferation between 20 hpf (20-somite stage) and 26 hpf with hydroxyurea and aphidicolin did not reduce the initial number of stc1+ cells that arise in the tubule nor does it block CS cell extrusion (n = 27/27, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from hydroxyurea and aphidicolin treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Inhibition of proliferation between 20 hpf and 26 hpf with hydroxyurea and aphidicolin does not block CS cell extrusion.
source: Inhibition of proliferation between 20 hpf (20-somite stage) and 26 hpf with hydroxyurea and aphidicolin did not reduce the initial number of stc1+ cells that arise in the tubule nor does it block CS cell extrusion (n = 27/27, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from hydroxyurea and aphidicolin treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Fewer stc1+ cells are observed in Blebbistatin-treated embryos at later stages compared to controls.
source: Consistent with CS cells undergoing cell division following their extrusion, fewer stc1+ cells were observed in Blebbistatin-treated embryos at later stages compared to controls, suggesting that there are two phases of CS cell formation: an intra-tubule transdifferentiation phase where a small number of CS cells are generated and a post-extrusion expansion phase.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations from Blebbistatin treatment.

claim: There are two phases of CS cell formation: an intra-tubule transdifferentiation phase where a small number of CS cells are generated and a post-extrusion expansion phase.
source: Consistent with CS cells undergoing cell division following their extrusion, fewer stc1+ cells were observed in Blebbistatin-treated embryos at later stages compared to controls, suggesting that there are two phases of CS cell formation: an intra-tubule transdifferentiation phase where a small number of CS cells are generated and a post-extrusion expansion phase.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from proliferation and Blebbistatin treatment experiments.

claim: Laser ablation to sever the tubule immediately anterior or posterior to the forming CS gland does not prevent CS extrusion (n = 6).
source: However, laser ablation to sever the tubule (and any interconnected contractile filaments) immediately anterior or posterior to the forming CS gland did not prevent CS extrusion (n = 6, Figure 2C), suggesting that neighbouring cells do not play an active role in CS extrusion.
evidence: The claim is supported by laser ablation experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Neighbouring cells do not play an active role in CS extrusion.
source: However, laser ablation to sever the tubule (and any interconnected contractile filaments) immediately anterior or posterior to the forming CS gland did not prevent CS extrusion (n = 6, Figure 2C), suggesting that neighbouring cells do not play an active role in CS extrusion.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the laser ablation experiment.

claim: Hnf1b is critical for establishing and maintaining renal epithelial cell fate.
source: We first examined Hnf1b as this transcription factor is critical for establishing and maintaining renal epithelial cell fate but is not expressed in the extruded CS gland ( (Naylor et al., 2013) and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Naylor et al., 2013).

claim: Hnf1b is not expressed in the extruded CS gland.
source: We first examined Hnf1b as this transcription factor is critical for establishing and maintaining renal epithelial cell fate but is not expressed in the extruded CS gland ( (Naylor et al., 2013) and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and cited literature.

claim: At 18 hpf, all cells in the renal tubule display nuclear localised Hnf1b (n = 7).
source: Immunostaining of embryos at 18 hpf showed that all cells in the renal tubule display nuclear localised Hnf1b (n = 7, Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: From 22 hpf onwards, Hnf1b is lost from the nucleus in presumptive CS cells and becomes localised to the cytoplasm in a speckled pattern (n = 9).
source: However, from 22 hpf onwards, we found that Hnf1b is lost from the nucleus in presumptive CS cells and becomes localised to the cytoplasm in a speckled pattern (n = 9, Figure 3A, see Figure 3—figure supplement 2 for lateral view).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cytoplasmic localisation of Hnf1b precedes the onset of stc1 expression.
source: As this cytoplasmic localisation of Hnf1b precedes the onset of stc1 expression, it suggests that loss of Hnf1b activity (via cytoplasmic sequestration) may be an early event in the transdifferentiation of renal to CS fate.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal sequence of Hnf1b localization and stc1 expression.

claim: Loss of Hnf1b activity (via cytoplasmic sequestration) may be an early event in the transdifferentiation of renal to CS fate.
source: As this cytoplasmic localisation of Hnf1b precedes the onset of stc1 expression, it suggests that loss of Hnf1b activity (via cytoplasmic sequestration) may be an early event in the transdifferentiation of renal to CS fate.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal sequence of Hnf1b localization and stc1 expression.

claim: In hnf1b-deficient embryos, a broad stretch of stc1 expression is detected in the middle of the pronephric tubule, largely corresponding to the region that would normally form the DE segment (n = 11/11).
source: In line with this, we detected a broad stretch of stc1 expression in the middle of the pronephric tubule, largely corresponding to the region that would normally form the DE segment (n = 11/11 hnf1b-deficient embryos, Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data from hnf1b-deficient embryos shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The formation of the DE segment has previously been shown to be regulated by the Irx3b transcription factor, which acts downstream of Hnf1b.
source: The formation of the DE segment has previously been shown to be regulated by the Irx3b transcription factor, which acts downstream of Hnf1b (Wingert and Davidson, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Wingert and Davidson, 2011).

claim: irx3b knockdown using morpholinos does not prevent the initial formation of the DE segment, as slc12a1 displays a normal expression pattern in irx3b morphants at 18 hpf (n = 21/21) and 20 hpf (n = 24/24).
source: We found that irx3b knockdown using morpholinos did not prevent the initial formation of the DE segment, as slc12a1 displays a normal expression pattern in irx3b morphants at 18 hpf (n = 21/21) and 20 hpf (n = 24/24, Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data from irx3b morphants shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The length of the DE segment is reduced in some irx3b-deficient embryos at 22 hpf (n = 14/23) and at 24 hpf (n = 19/25) compared to control embryos (n = 0/21 at 22 hpf and n = 0/43 at 24 hpf).
source: However, we noted that the length of the DE segment was reduced in some irx3b-deficient embryos at 22 hpf (n = 14/23) and at 24 hpf (n = 19/25, Figure 4A) compared to control embryos (n = 0/21 at 22 hpf and n = 0/43 at 24 hpf) and there was a corresponding expansion in stc1+ CS cells from 24 hpf onwards (Figure 4B, Table 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data from irx3b-deficient embryos shown in Figure 4A.

claim: There is a corresponding expansion in stc1+ CS cells from 24 hpf onwards in irx3b-deficient embryos.
source: However, we noted that the length of the DE segment was reduced in some irx3b-deficient embryos at 22 hpf (n = 14/23) and at 24 hpf (n = 19/25, Figure 4A) compared to control embryos (n = 0/21 at 22 hpf and n = 0/43 at 24 hpf) and there was a corresponding expansion in stc1+ CS cells from 24 hpf onwards (Figure 4B, Table 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4B and Table 1.

claim: By 36 hpf, the DE region in irx3b-deficient embryos lacks transcripts for slc12a1.
source: By 36 hpf, the DE region lacked transcripts for slc12a1, consistent with previous reports (Wingert and Davidson, 2011) and cdh17 was down-regulated in the region where ectopic stc1+ cells are present (Figure 4B, Table 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4B and cited literature.

claim: By 36 hpf, cdh17 is down-regulated in the region where ectopic stc1+ cells are present in irx3b-deficient embryos.
source: By 36 hpf, the DE region lacked transcripts for slc12a1, consistent with previous reports (Wingert and Davidson, 2011) and cdh17 was down-regulated in the region where ectopic stc1+ cells are present (Figure 4B, Table 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4B and Table 1.

claim: Ectopic CS cells in irx3b-deficient animals still undergo apical constriction but are not fully extruded from the tubule.
source: An analysis of live Tg(cdh17:egfp) embryos that are deficient in irx3b showed that these ectopic CS cells still underwent apical constriction but were not fully extruded from the tubule (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data from irx3b-deficient embryos shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The tubule cells rostral to the enlarged CS gland display a stretched morphology in irx3b-deficient animals.
source: In addition, we found that the tubule cells rostral to the enlarged CS gland display a stretched morphology in irx3b-deficient animals, both in live Tg(cdh17:egfp) embryos (Figure 5A) and by expression analysis of the pan-tubule marker atp1a1a.4 (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The DL segment is compacted and shorter in irx3b-depleted animals.
source: Conversely, the DL segment was compacted and shorter in irx3b-depleted animals (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The tubule starts moving rostrally by 29 hpf.
source: Given that the tubule starts moving rostrally by 29 hpf (Vasilyev et al., 2009), the morphological effects caused by irx3b knockdown suggests that an enlarged and un-extruded CS gland may prevent the DL segment from undergoing this movement, resulting in greater stretching of the more proximal tubule cells and compaction of the distal tubule.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Vasilyev et al., 2009).

claim: An enlarged and un-extruded CS gland may prevent the DL segment from undergoing rostral movement, resulting in greater stretching of the more proximal tubule cells and compaction of the distal tubule.
source: Given that the tubule starts moving rostrally by 29 hpf (Vasilyev et al., 2009), the morphological effects caused by irx3b knockdown suggests that an enlarged and un-extruded CS gland may prevent the DL segment from undergoing this movement, resulting in greater stretching of the more proximal tubule cells and compaction of the distal tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed morphological effects in irx3b-deficient embryos.

claim: The majority of irx3b-deficient animals treated with Blebbistatin display relatively normal tubule morphology with ectopic stc1+ cells scattered throughout the tubule (n = 20/25).
source: To test this, irx3b-deficient animals were treated with Blebbistatin to block apical constriction. The majority of these animals were found to display relatively normal tubule morphology with ectopic stc1+ cells scattered throughout the tubule (n = 20/25, Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from combined irx3b knockdown and Blebbistatin treatment shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Irx3b inhibits the transdifferentiation of DE cells to a CS fate.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Irx3b inhibits the transdifferentiation of DE cells to a CS fate and that the failed extrusion of the ectopic CS cells seen in irx3b-deficient embryos alters tubular cell morphology due to a block in the rostral migration of the DL segment.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experiments with irx3b-deficient embryos.

claim: The failed extrusion of the ectopic CS cells seen in irx3b-deficient embryos alters tubular cell morphology due to a block in the rostral migration of the DL segment.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Irx3b inhibits the transdifferentiation of DE cells to a CS fate and that the failed extrusion of the ectopic CS cells seen in irx3b-deficient embryos alters tubular cell morphology due to a block in the rostral migration of the DL segment.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experiments combining irx3b knockdown and Blebbistatin treatment.

claim: The Irx factors have been implicated as both positive and negative regulators of Notch signalling.
source: We then went on to examine a link between Irx3b and Notch, as the Irx factors have been implicated as both positive and negative regulators of Notch signalling (Scarlett et al., 2015; Domínguez and de Celis, 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Scarlett et al., 2015; Domínguez and de Celis, 1998).

claim: Notch has recently been connected to CS gland development.
source: In addition, Notch has recently been connected to CS gland development (Drummond et al., 2017) and Notch components are expressed in CS cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Drummond et al., 2017).

claim: Notch components are expressed in CS cells.
source: In addition, Notch has recently been connected to CS gland development (Drummond et al., 2017) and Notch components are expressed in CS cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Notch activity is found in CS cells from 36 hpf onwards.
source: We first analysed the TP1:VenusPEST Notch reporter line, which contains multiple RBP-Jk-binding sites in front of a minimal promoter (Ninov et al., 2012), and found Notch activity in CS cells from 36 hpf onwards (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 6A and cited literature.

claim: The Notch pathway plays a role in CS gland formation.
source: This result is consistent with the Notch pathway playing a role in CS gland formation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the Notch reporter activity in CS cells.

claim: Treatment with cpdE from 18 hpf onwards results in reduced numbers of stc1+ cells (n = 56/56).
source: To assess the functional consequences of loss of Notch signalling, we treated wild-type zebrafish embryos with the γ-secretase inhibitor compound E (cpdE, Figure 6B) or DAPT (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A) from 18 hpf onwards and found reduced numbers of stc1+ cells (n = 56/56 in cpdE treated, n = 29/31 in DAPT treated).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from cpdE treatment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Treatment with DAPT from 18 hpf onwards results in reduced numbers of stc1+ cells (n = 29/31).
source: To assess the functional consequences of loss of Notch signalling, we treated wild-type zebrafish embryos with the γ-secretase inhibitor compound E (cpdE, Figure 6B) or DAPT (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A) from 18 hpf onwards and found reduced numbers of stc1+ cells (n = 56/56 in cpdE treated, n = 29/31 in DAPT treated).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from DAPT treatment shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Treatment with cpdE from 10 hpf onwards paradoxically increases the size of the CS gland (n = 21/29).
source: However, as reported previously (Drummond et al., 2017), treatment with cpdE (n = 21/29) or DAPT (n = 20/34) from 10 hpf onwards paradoxically increased the size of the CS gland (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), indicating that perturbation of Notch signalling has complex temporal effects on CS formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from cpdE treatment shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B and cited literature.

claim: Treatment with DAPT from 10 hpf onwards paradoxically increases the size of the CS gland (n = 20/34).
source: However, as reported previously (Drummond et al., 2017), treatment with cpdE (n = 21/29) or DAPT (n = 20/34) from 10 hpf onwards paradoxically increased the size of the CS gland (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), indicating that perturbation of Notch signalling has complex temporal effects on CS formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from DAPT treatment shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B and cited literature.

claim: Perturbation of Notch signalling has complex temporal effects on CS formation.
source: However, as reported previously (Drummond et al., 2017), treatment with cpdE (n = 21/29) or DAPT (n = 20/34) from 10 hpf onwards paradoxically increased the size of the CS gland (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), indicating that perturbation of Notch signalling has complex temporal effects on CS formation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the different effects of Notch inhibition at different developmental stages.

claim: Injection of two gRNAs targeting irx3b reproduced the irx3b morpholino phenotype in F0 animals (crispants) by increasing the number of stc1+ cells in the DE region of the tubule (n = 45/49).
source: Injection of two gRNAs targeting irx3b reproduced the irx3b morpholino phenotype in F0 animals (crispants) by increasing the number of stc1+ cells in the DE region of the tubule (n = 45/49, Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by CRISPR-Cas9 experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: T7 endonuclease 1 analysis for DNA mismatches in irx3b crispants indicated successful mutagenesis was achieved.
source: T7 endonuclease 1 analysis (Huang et al., 2012) for DNA mismatches in irx3b crispants indicated successful mutagenesis was achieved (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by T7 endonuclease assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Stable mutant lines with a frame-shift deletion allele phenocopied the morphant/crispant phenotypes.
source: These crispant embryos were also grown to adulthood and used to generate stable mutant lines with a frame-shift deletion allele that similarly phenocopied the morphant/crispant phenotypes (Figure 6—figure supplement 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from stable mutant lines shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4B and C.

claim: irx3b crispants treated with cpdE from 18 to 50 hpf show a robust reduction in the number of stc1+ cells (n = 37/37).
source: We found that irx3b crispants treated with cpdE from 18 to 50 hpf showed a robust reduction in the number of stc1+ cells (n = 37/37; Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from combined irx3b CRISPR and cpdE treatment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Irx3b acts upstream or in parallel to late (18 hpf onwards) Notch signalling to inhibit the transdifferentiation of DE cells into CS cells.
source: Thus, we conclude that Irx3b acts upstream or in parallel to late (18 hpf onwards) Notch signalling to inhibit the transdifferentiation of DE cells into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from epistasis experiments combining irx3b knockdown and Notch inhibition.

claim: In irx3b crispants at 50 hpf, the number of cells with nuclear-localised Hnf1b is quantitatively decreased in the region of the DE segment that shows unextruded CS cells.
source: We found in irx3b crispants at 50 hpf that the number of cells with nuclear-localised Hnf1b was quantitatively decreased in the region of the DE segment that shows unextruded CS cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: In wild-type (n = 27/27) or irx3b crispant embryos (n = 25/25) treated with cpdE, Hnf1b is retained in the nucleus of renal tubule cells in the DE region.
source: In contrast, in wild-type (n = 27/27) or irx3b crispant embryos (n = 25/25) that had been treated with cpdE Hnf1b was retained in the nucleus of renal tubule cells in the DE region (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: Treatment with cpdE reduces the TP1:VenusPEST fluorescence in control (n = 28/28) and irx3b crispants (n = 32/45).
source: Treatment with cpdE also reduced the TP1:VenusPEST fluorescence in control (n = 28/28) and irx3b crispants (n = 32/45) consistent with the inhibitory effects of cpdE on CS cell formation being mediated by a block in Notch-Rbpj signal transduction (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 6B and 6D.

claim: The inhibitory effects of cpdE on CS cell formation are mediated by a block in Notch-Rbpj signal transduction.
source: Treatment with cpdE also reduced the TP1:VenusPEST fluorescence in control (n = 28/28) and irx3b crispants (n = 32/45) consistent with the inhibitory effects of cpdE on CS cell formation being mediated by a block in Notch-Rbpj signal transduction (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the correlation between reduced reporter activity and reduced CS cell formation.

claim: Notch signalling and the cytoplasmic sequestration of Hnf1b in a subset of DE epithelial cells leads to the transdifferentiation of renal epithelial cells into CS cells.
source: Together, these results support a model in which Notch signalling and the cytoplasmic sequestration of Hnf1b in a subset of DE epithelial cells leads to the transdifferentiation of renal epithelial cells into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experiments examining Notch signalling, Hnf1b localization, and CS cell formation.

claim: The transdifferentiation of DE to CS fate occurs in sequential steps.
source: Our data indicate that the transdifferentiation of DE to CS fate occurs in sequential steps and the finding that CS cell numbers are reduced by pharmacological inhibition of Notch signalling from 18 hpf onwards, just prior to the appearance of stc1+ cells, suggests that the Notch pathway plays an early instructive role.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal sequence of events and Notch inhibition experiments.

claim: The Notch pathway plays an early instructive role in CS cell formation.
source: Our data indicate that the transdifferentiation of DE to CS fate occurs in sequential steps and the finding that CS cell numbers are reduced by pharmacological inhibition of Notch signalling from 18 hpf onwards, just prior to the appearance of stc1+ cells, suggests that the Notch pathway plays an early instructive role.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the timing of Notch inhibition effects.

claim: Notch has well-described roles in determining binary cell fate decisions during progenitor cell decisions including in the zebrafish pronephros where it acts by a classical lateral-inhibition mechanism to inhibit a multi-ciliated phenotype in renal progenitors.
source: Notch has well-described roles in determining binary cell fate decisions during progenitor cell decisions including in the zebrafish pronephros where it acts by a classical lateral-inhibition mechanism to inhibit a multi-ciliated phenotype in renal progenitors (Liu et al., 2007; Ma and Jiang, 2007; Marra and Wingert, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Liu et al., 2007; Ma and Jiang, 2007; Marra and Wingert, 2016).

claim: A similar lateral-inhibition pathway may be required for the DE-to-CS transdifferentiation but with the timing of this occurring after the multi-ciliated cell fate decision.
source: A similar lateral-inhibition pathway may be required for the DE-to-CS transdifferentiation but with the timing of this occurring after the multi-ciliated cell fate decision (Wingert et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2007; Ma and Jiang, 2007).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on analogy to known Notch functions.

claim: Notch is implicated in the conversion of rectal epithelial Y cells into motor neurons in C. elegans, although in this case the Y cell transitions to an intermediary cell state rather than directly transdifferentiating.
source: In the context of transdifferentiation, work in C. elegans has implicated Notch in the conversion of rectal epithelial Y cells into motor neurons, although in this case the Y cell transitions to an intermediary cell state rather than directly transdifferentiating as seen in our study (Jarriault et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Jarriault et al., 2008).

claim: In adult mice, bronchial 'club' cells, which depend on active Notch for their maintenance, switch to a ciliated phenotype following disruption of Notch signalling, without an apparent dedifferentiation stage or need for cell division.
source: In a mammalian example, bronchial cells known as 'club' cells, which depend on active Notch for their maintenance, switch to a ciliated phenotype following disruption of Notch signalling in adult mice, without an apparent dedifferentiation stage or need for cell division (Lafkas et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Lafkas et al., 2015).

claim: The Hnf1b transcription factor becomes sequestered in the cytoplasm of cells undergoing transdifferentiation.
source: Our observation that the Hnf1b transcription factor, a master regulator of renal epithelial fate, becomes sequestered in the cytoplasm of cells undergoing transdifferentiation suggests that Notch regulates the levels of Hnf1b in the nucleus either by inducing Hnf1b nuclear export or alternatively, if the nuclear turnover of Hnf1b is high, by preventing newly translated Hnf1b from entering the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Notch regulates the levels of Hnf1b in the nucleus either by inducing Hnf1b nuclear export or by preventing newly translated Hnf1b from entering the nucleus.
source: Our observation that the Hnf1b transcription factor, a master regulator of renal epithelial fate, becomes sequestered in the cytoplasm of cells undergoing transdifferentiation suggests that Notch regulates the levels of Hnf1b in the nucleus either by inducing Hnf1b nuclear export or alternatively, if the nuclear turnover of Hnf1b is high, by preventing newly translated Hnf1b from entering the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing possible mechanisms for Hnf1b cytoplasmic localization.

claim: Hnf1b is considered a relatively stable 'bookmarking' factor that remains associated with chromatin during cell division where it reinstates transcriptional programs following mitotic exit.
source: We favour the former notion as Hnf1b is considered a relatively stable 'bookmarking' factor that remains associated with chromatin during cell division where it reinstates transcriptional programs following mitotic exit (Verdeguer et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Verdeguer et al., 2010).

claim: Hnf1b is critical for renal tubule differentiation in zebrafish and mice.
source: As Hnf1b is critical for renal tubule differentiation in zebrafish and mice (Naylor et al., 2013; Heliot et al., 2013; Massa et al., 2013; Naylor and Davidson, 2014), we hypothesise that there is an on-going requirement for Hnf1b in the tubule to maintain renal epithelial identity and that sequestration of this factor is sufficient to induce the transdifferentiation of DE cells into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Naylor et al., 2013; Heliot et al., 2013; Massa et al., 2013; Naylor and Davidson, 2014).

claim: There is an on-going requirement for Hnf1b in the tubule to maintain renal epithelial identity and sequestration of this factor is sufficient to induce the transdifferentiation of DE cells into CS cells.
source: As Hnf1b is critical for renal tubule differentiation in zebrafish and mice (Naylor et al., 2013; Heliot et al., 2013; Massa et al., 2013; Naylor and Davidson, 2014), we hypothesise that there is an on-going requirement for Hnf1b in the tubule to maintain renal epithelial identity and that sequestration of this factor is sufficient to induce the transdifferentiation of DE cells into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on inference from Hnf1b's known role and the observed cytoplasmic sequestration.

claim: The Notch ligand jagged-2a is abnormally maintained in the pronephric tubule of hnf1b-deficient embryos.
source: Whether CS identity is a default state in the tubule is unclear, but we have observed that the Notch ligand jagged-2a is abnormally maintained in the pronephric tubule of hnf1b-deficient embryos (data not shown) consistent with aberrant Notch signalling also being involved in the induction of ectopic stc1.
evidence: The claim is supported by unpublished data mentioned in the text.

claim: Aberrant Notch signalling is involved in the induction of ectopic stc1 in hnf1b-deficient embryos.
source: Whether CS identity is a default state in the tubule is unclear, but we have observed that the Notch ligand jagged-2a is abnormally maintained in the pronephric tubule of hnf1b-deficient embryos (data not shown) consistent with aberrant Notch signalling also being involved in the induction of ectopic stc1.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the abnormal maintenance of jagged-2a in hnf1b-deficient embryos.

claim: hnf1b-deficient embryos fail to express irx3b in the renal tubules.
source: We have previously linked Hnf1b and Irx3b together by demonstrating that hnf1b-deficient embryos fail to express irx3b in the renal tubules (Naylor et al., 2013), placing hnf1b upstream of irx3b in a genetic hierarchy.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Naylor et al., 2013).

claim: hnf1b is upstream of irx3b in a genetic hierarchy.
source: We have previously linked Hnf1b and Irx3b together by demonstrating that hnf1b-deficient embryos fail to express irx3b in the renal tubules (Naylor et al., 2013), placing hnf1b upstream of irx3b in a genetic hierarchy.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the loss of irx3b expression in hnf1b-deficient embryos.

claim: irx3b deficiency does not influence the initial specification of the DE segment but instead leads to the dramatic transdifferentiation of this segment into CS cells.
source: In this study we show that irx3b deficiency does not influence the initial specification of the DE segment as previously thought (Wingert and Davidson, 2011) but instead leads to the dramatic transdifferentiation of this segment into CS cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from irx3b-deficient embryos described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The ectopic CS cells in irx3b-deficient embryos display cytoplasmic Hnf1b.
source: Consistent with our notion that Hnf1b sequestration drives this transdifferentiation, we found that the ectopic CS cells display cytoplasmic Hnf1b.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Inhibiting Notch signalling rescued the CS expansion phenotype in irx3b-deficient animals, including Hnf1b nuclear localisation.
source: Furthermore, inhibiting Notch signalling rescued the CS expansion phenotype in irx3b-deficient animals, including Hnf1b nuclear localisation, placing Irx3b upstream or in parallel to the Notch pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from combined irx3b knockdown and Notch inhibition described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Irx/Iroquois family transcription factors have been reported to modulate Notch signalling in other cellular contexts.
source: Irx/Iroquois family transcription factors have been reported to modulate Notch signalling in other cellular contexts.
evidence: The claim is based on general knowledge about Irx/Iroquois transcription factors.

claim: During Drosophila eye development, the Iroquois genes establish where Notch activation occurs by controlling the levels of Fringe, a glycosyltransferase that alters the sensitivity of the Notch receptors to transactivation from the different classes of Notch ligand.
source: Most notably during Drosophila eye development, where the Iroquois genes establish where Notch activation occurs by controlling the levels of Fringe, a glycosyltransferase that alters the sensitivity of the Notch receptors to transactivation from the different classes of Notch ligand (Panin et al., 1997; Moloney et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Panin et al., 1997; Moloney et al., 2000).

claim: In vertebrates, including zebrafish, there are three Fringe homologues.
source: In vertebrates, including zebrafish, there are three Fringe homologues (Qiu et al., 2004) but their expression patterns during CS formation have not been closely examined.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Qiu et al., 2004).

claim: Irx3b may modulate Notch signalling in the DE segment via the regulation of fringe or other Notch pathway genes, to ensure that the CS-inducing effects of Notch signalling are suppressed.
source: One speculative idea is that Irx3b modulates Notch signalling in the DE segment via the regulation of fringe or other Notch pathway genes, to ensure that the CS-inducing effects of Notch signalling are suppressed.
evidence: The claim is explicitly speculative, proposing a possible mechanism.

claim: Cross-regulatory interactions between Notch and Irx3 have been shown in human microvascular endothelial cells where Irx3 induces expression of Delta-like ligand four but is in turn repressed by the Notch mediator Hey1 via direct binding to the Irx3 promoter.
source: It is also interesting to note that cross-regulatory interactions between Notch and Irx3 have been shown in human microvascular endothelial cells where Irx3 induces expression of Delta-like ligand four but is in turn repressed by the Notch mediator Hey1 via direct binding to the Irx3 promoter (Scarlett et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Scarlett et al., 2015).

claim: Apical constriction is a well-known feature of polarised epithelia that drives bending, folding and tube formation during the formation of different tissues and organs.
source: Apical constriction is a well-known feature of polarised epithelia that drives bending, folding and tube formation during the formation of different tissues and organs (Sawyer et al., 2010; Martin et al., 2009a; Mason et al., 2013; Sadler, 2005; Martin and Goldstein, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Sawyer et al., 2010; Martin et al., 2009a; Mason et al., 2013; Sadler, 2005; Martin and Goldstein, 2014).

claim: Apical constriction is driven by contraction of an apical meshwork of F-actin by the molecular motor myosin IIA.
source: Apical constriction is driven by contraction of an apical meshwork of F-actin by the molecular motor myosin IIA (Martin et al., 2009b) and consistent with this, we found that blebbistatin treatment inhibited CS cell extrusion.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Martin et al., 2009b) and experimental data from blebbistatin treatment.

claim: In the Drosophila eye-antennal disc, Notch activation has been found to trigger actomyosin-mediated cell apical constriction.

evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Ku and Sun, 2017).

claim: The Notch pathway may both induce DE-to-CS transdifferentiation and initiate apical constriction.
source: Interestingly, in the Drosophila eye-antennal disc, Notch activation has been found to trigger actomyosin-mediated cell apical constriction, raising the possibility that the Notch pathway may both induce DE-to-CS transdifferentiation and initiate apical constriction (Ku and Sun, 2017).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on analogy to Drosophila.

claim: In the developing avian lung, the tubular epithelium of the primary bronchus undergoes apical constriction in localised areas, resulting in the formation of lung buds that then grow out as new airways.
source: In the developing avian lung, where the tubular epithelium of the primary bronchus undergoes apical constriction in localised areas, the result is the formation of lung buds that then grow out as new airways (Locy WA, 1916).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Locy WA, 1916).

claim: The 'bud' of CS cells is made up of far fewer cells than lung buds, does not transition to a tubular outgrowth, and proliferation is not required for its extrusion.
source: Unlike this system, the 'bud' of CS cells we observe is made up of far fewer cells, does not transition to a tubular outgrowth and proliferation is not required for its extrusion, although we do observe CS cells proliferating once they are free from the tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with lung budding and experimental data from proliferation studies.

claim: CS cells proliferate once they are free from the tubule.
source: Unlike this system, the 'bud' of CS cells we observe is made up of far fewer cells, does not transition to a tubular outgrowth and proliferation is not required for its extrusion, although we do observe CS cells proliferating once they are free from the tubule.

claim: The budding CS cells are 'shed' basally, en masse, as an intact ball of cells.
source: Instead, the budding CS cells are 'shed' basally, en masse, as an intact ball of cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: While apical constriction initiates the CS extrusion process, additional cellular behaviours must be required to extrude the cells.
source: Thus, we conclude that while apical constriction initiates the process, additional cellular behaviours must then be required to extrude the cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that apical constriction alone does not fully explain the extrusion process.

claim: In the pancreas, the primitive duct epithelium responds to low Notch signalling to down-regulate Cdh1 in single cells that then undergo EMT and delaminate as endocrine precursors.
source: This is an attractive hypothesis, particularly given that this process operates in other related tissues such as the pancreas, where the primitive duct epithelium responds to low Notch signalling to down-regulate Cdh1 in single cells that then undergo EMT and delaminate as endocrine precursors (Shih et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Shih et al., 2012).

claim: CS cells do not undergo a loss of Cdh1 during extrusion.
source: However, we do not observe a loss of Cdh1, which is a widely used definition of EMT (Kalluri and Weinberg, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: No intermediary mesenchyme-like state is captured during CS cell extrusion.
source: Furthermore, from our histological analysis we have not been able to capture an intermediary mesenchyme-like state and observe no migration of individual CS cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of observed intermediary states in histological analysis.

source: Based on this, we favour a model in which CS cells are extruded by a non-EMT-based pathway that may be more comparable to the epithelial remodelling that occurs during primary spinal cord formation in the embryo.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed characteristics of CS cell extrusion and comparison to neural tube closure.

claim: During neural tube closure, the neural plate undergoes apical constriction and invaginates before pinching off as the neural tube while the surrounding non-neural ectoderm fuses together.
source: Here, the neural plate undergoes apical constriction and invaginates before pinching off as the neural tube while the surrounding non-neural ectoderm fuses together (Nikolopoulou et al., 2017).

evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Ray and Niswander, 2016).

claim: Overcrowding of epithelial sheets results in live cell extrusion of single cells by a mechanism that involves the formation of an actomyosin contractile ring in cells surrounding the extruded cell.
source: Prior work has shown that overcrowding of epithelial sheets results in live cell extrusion of single cells by a mechanism that involves the formation of an actomyosin contractile ring in cells surrounding the extruded cell. This ring then contracts and the innermost cell is pushed out of the epithelium (Eisenhoffer et al., 2012; Gu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Eisenhoffer et al., 2012; Gu et al., 2011).

claim: Treating embryos with the S1P2 receptor inhibitor JTE-013 has no effect on CS extrusion.

evidence: The claim is supported by unpublished data mentioned in the text.

claim: The mechanism of live cell extrusion involving actomyosin contractile rings in neighbouring cells is unlikely to be playing a role in CS gland shedding.
source: Thus, it is unlikely that this mechanism of live cell extrusion is playing a role in CS gland shedding.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from laser ablation and drug treatment experiments.

claim: The conversion of DE cells to a CS gland fate in the zebrafish renal tubule represents a novel example of a developmentally programmed direct transdifferentiation event coupled to an unusual live cell extrusion behaviour.
source: Taken together, our data show that the conversion of DE cells to a CS gland fate in the zebrafish renal tubule represents a novel example of a developmentally programmed direct transdifferentiation event coupled to an unusual live cell extrusion behaviour.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on all the data presented in the study.
